title: Journey document
description: journey.yaml — one actor's path across the solution, in order: a flat list of 2 to 12 steps, no ids, no branches. Specified in framework/spec/kinds/journey.md; parsed by framework/portal/src/lib/journey/journey.ts.

$schema.description: The dialect discriminator (0015-artifact-dialects); the canonical value is this schema's own $id. Deliberately unpinned rather than const: a value naming some other dialect is W_ARTIFACT_DIALECT, a warning, read as the legacy dialect and never broken — a const here would restate that ruling as a hard rejection in the one place a severity cannot be relaxed. The loader strips the key before parseJourney is handed the document, so nothing in the catalog depends on the parser tolerating it. parseJourney admits it regardless: $schema is listed in KNOWN_FILE_KEYS beside name and steps, at the top level only, so a caller holding raw file bytes and no loader — a fixture, an editor, a consumer reading this schema — gets the legacy dialect read rather than E_JRN_SCHEMA on the header this schema tells them to write. Admitted by name and not by widening the x- hatch: x- is the author's namespace and stays open-ended, $schema is one framework-owned literal, so the parser's set of legal top-level keys grew by exactly one and every other unknown key is still an error.

name.description: MUST equal the entity's name, i.e. its directory name (E_JRN_NAME) — the filename is fixed, so it carries no identity. Checked against the entity and never against the filename stem: a file copied into the wrong entity directory says so instead of silently becoming that entity's path.

^x-.description: The escape hatch reaches into this artifact, at the top level and inside a step. Tolerated and ignored by the portal; any other unknown key is E_JRN_SCHEMA. There is no title and no summary — index.md already carries both, and a second copy in the artifact would only drift — and no top-level version: the entity's frontmatter governs the whole directory.

steps.description: The list order IS the order: no order key, no step ids, no timestamps, no durations. Both bounds are errors and not warnings (E_JRN_STEP_COUNT) — one step is a touch rather than a path, twelve rows is where the derived ladder stops fitting one screen, and a cap that only warns is a cap every catalog eventually ignores. The portal's stable key for a step is its positional path, steps[3], 0-based.

step.description: A described position, not an observed event. Exactly four keys are recognised, and each step carries its own subject: actor is written on every step rather than defaulting from the frontmatter protagonist, because a hand-off is the row a reader most needs to see and a field that defaults is a field that hides its exceptions.

actor.description: Who takes this step. MUST resolve to an entity of kind actor (E_JRN_ACTOR_KIND). The frontmatter protagonist MUST be the actor of at least one step (W_JRN_ACTOR_ABSENT); every other actor here is a counterpart the path hands off to or waits on.

touches.description: What they touch. MUST resolve to a component or a product (E_JRN_TOUCHES_KIND). Its owning product — the product/{name} pair at the head of the pair chain — is what makes a product crossing decidable from the grammar alone.

protocol.description: How the step reaches what it touches. Three states, not two: an SRN resolving to a protocol (E_JRN_PROTOCOL_KIND); the literal none, the documented negative, meaning the actor carries the crossing and there is nothing to write down; or omitted, meaning not written down yet — which on a product crossing is W_JRN_UNDOCUMENTED_INTEGRATION, the check the kind exists for.

note.description: One line, display only, rendered as a note anchored to the step. The place a fork in the path is named, since the second branch is a second journey.

not.description: A journey is exactly one linear sequence. A branch-shaped key gets its own error class (E_JRN_BRANCH) rather than the generic E_JRN_SCHEMA, because the code is the lesson: a journey that branches is two journeys. The distinction is a diagnostic class and not a validity difference, so this clause restates a rejection additionalProperties already makes — what it adds is the seven names.

srn-ref.description: An ordinary SRN reference, absolute or relative, resolved from the entity's own directory and never crossing into another solution. A journey sits at solution level and points almost entirely outward, so the solution-absolute form (/product/shop/component/checkout) is the readable one everywhere. Version pins parse but SHOULD be omitted — a pinned component would freeze the description of a thing that is still moving. An artifact suffix is refused on every step field (JRN16): a step means an entity, and an artifact has no kind.
